implementation_statement: Joiner and leaver events flow automatically from the HR system to the identity provider; group-based provisioning to federated applications.

implementation_statement: The TOS enforces role-based access (planner, superintendent, gate clerk, billing, administrator) for both terminals. Customs hold overrides require the superintendent role. The portal enforces trucking company tenancy. Cloud access uses provider IAM roles assigned from directory groups.
evidence: TOS role matrix; portal tenancy tests; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: T1: an industrial firewall separates the OT zone (cranes, RTGs, crane management system, reefer monitoring) and allows only the TOS equipment interface, VMT and maintenance flows. Gap: T2 has no information flow enforcement between the gate network and mobile harbor crane controllers.
evidence: T1 OT firewall rule set; T2 switch configuration

implementation_statement: Separation of duties between TOS administration, billing and customs hold overrides is defined in the TOS role matrix. Gap: the 5 TOS application staff can both change and release portal code (P07 SA-11).
evidence: TOS role matrix; code repository permissions

implementation_statement: Standard users have no local administrator rights on managed endpoints. Gaps: 9 standing domain administrator accounts; shared OT engineering accounts on cranes at both terminals; privileged access management only for the cloud (P07 AC-6).
evidence: Directory privileged group export; OT account list

implementation_statement: IT administrators have separate administrator accounts for cloud and directory work. Gap: OT engineering accounts are used for both routine and privileged functions.
Cloud privileged roles use just-in-time elevation through the privileged access broker. Gap: directory, identity provider and TOS administrator roles are standing.
The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts; the VPN authenticates through the identity provider. Gap: T2 gate servers and OT HMIs have no lockout.
evidence: Identity provider policy; T2 gate server local policy

implementation_statement: Managed endpoints lock after 10 minutes. Gap: T2 gate booth workstations and HMIs do not lock.
Identity provider sessions end after 12 hours or on sign-out; TOS sessions time out after 30 minutes idle.

implementation_statement: Staff remote access uses the VPN with identity provider MFA. The T1 crane OEM connects only through the privileged remote access service with MFA and session recording. Gaps: the T2 mobile harbor crane OEM uses an always-on cellular appliance with a shared account; the OCR and reefer monitoring vendors use their own remote tools (P07 AC-17).
evidence: VPN configuration; remote access service logs; T2 walkthrough

implementation_statement: T1 VMT Wi-Fi uses WPA2-Enterprise with device certificates inside the OT zone. Gap: T2 VMT Wi-Fi uses a pre-shared key bridged into the flat gate and yard network.

Vendor technician laptops may connect to OT only by exception. Gap: at T2 crane technicians connect their own laptops to HMIs without a scan or approval.
evidence: Interview Director of Maintenance and Engineering; T2 walkthrough
